item.title: Friday 27 November: BoE cuts bank capital
item.description: The Bank of England cuts UK bank capital requirements by about 50bp and flags $4trn of AI exposure; euro area backs Hernández de Cos for ECB president; S&P reviews France tonight.
item.itunes:summary: The Bank of England cuts UK bank capital requirements by about 50bp and flags $4trn of AI exposure; euro area backs Hernández de Cos for ECB president; S&P reviews France tonight.

item.title: Thursday 26 November: Hot Inflation, Thanksgiving Calm
item.description: Core PCE hits a three-year high as Treasuries rally anyway, the Bank of England publishes its Financial Stability Report, and the Bank of Korea hikes to 3.25%.
item.itunes:summary: Core PCE hits a three-year high as Treasuries rally anyway, the Bank of England publishes its Financial Stability Report, and the Bank of Korea hikes to 3.25%.

item.title: Wednesday 25 November: AI trade cracks again
item.description: Nvidia and Asian chip stocks slide as Anthropic falls below its IPO price; FDIC shows US bank unrealised losses up almost 50% to $486bn; markets price a December Fed hike ahead of today's PCE.
item.itunes:summary: Nvidia and Asian chip stocks slide as Anthropic falls below its IPO price; FDIC shows US bank unrealised losses up almost 50% to $486bn; markets price a December Fed hike ahead of today's PCE.

item.title: Tuesday 24 November: Huang returns, Irca deal hangs
item.description: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang sparks a 4.7% S&P rebound, UBS, Barclays, BNP and HSBC are left holding €1.2bn of Irca debt after CVC walks away, and Fed's Williams keeps a December hike in play.

item.title: Monday 23 November: Wall Street enters correction
item.description: The S&P 500 falls into a correction as bank stocks post their worst week since April 2025, Anthropic's stock tests its IPO price, and HSBC refinances its AT1 at 7.625% while Asia rolls out market-support measures.

item.title: Friday 20 November: Banks hit death cross
item.description: Wall Street sell-off drags US banks into a death cross, Anthropic closes 17% up after a faded debut, and the ECB keeps 2027 capital requirements broadly flat.
item.itunes:summary: Wall Street sell-off drags US banks into a death cross, Anthropic closes 17% up after a faded debut, and the ECB keeps 2027 capital requirements broadly flat.

item.title: Thursday 19 November: Anthropic prices record IPO
item.description: Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at 83 dollars, Fed hawks lift the dollar and yields, and Deutsche Bank faces a data-protection probe as UniCredit settles Commerzbank terms with Berlin.
item.itunes:summary: Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at 83 dollars, Fed hawks lift the dollar and yields, and Deutsche Bank faces a data-protection probe as UniCredit settles Commerzbank terms with Berlin.

item.title: Wednesday 18 November: Deutsche Bank files leak
item.description: Leaked files hit Deutsche Bank shares, ING and SocGen sell data-centre loans as US chip curbs freeze a ByteDance-linked loan, and UBS looks set to lose its Swiss capital fight.
item.itunes:summary: Leaked files hit Deutsche Bank shares, ING and SocGen sell data-centre loans as US chip curbs freeze a ByteDance-linked loan, and UBS looks set to lose its Swiss capital fight.

item.title: Tuesday 17 November: AI loan gets a price
item.description: HSBC sells a slice of an Oracle-linked data-centre loan in the mid-80s, Brussels clears UniCredit-Commerzbank unconditionally, and US bank outages hit shares as the Nasdaq enters correction ahead of Nvidia and Anthropic.

item.title: Monday 16 November: New World tests its banks
item.description: New World Development's deeply discounted rights issue and bank loan extension, record first halves and buybacks at the Japanese megabanks, and the Fed's warning on nearly one trillion dollars of bank exposure to the AI build-out.

item.title: Friday 13 November: Bonds Bite, Nvidia Shock
item.description: Ten-year Treasury closes near 5.1% as cash bonds reopen; Jensen Huang quits Nvidia, jolting the AI-lending trade; Banco BPM opens talks with Credit Agricole on control-premium terms.

item.description: ABN AMRO beats with 940 million euros of profit and higher NII guidance, the US bond market reopens after a hot CPI print with a December Fed hike priced, and Credit Agricole's Banco BPM merger proposal plus the UniCredit-Commerzbank EU deadline drive Italian and German bank M&A.

item.title: Wednesday 11 November: Hot CPI, Fed hike talk
